subject: wood frog
title: This Frog Freezes Solid Every Winter, and Its Heart Stops

scenes.text: This frog dies every winter and comes back every spring.
At the first sign of ice, a wood frog freezes solid. Its heart stops. Its breathing stops.
Ice grows around its organs for months, while a sugar antifreeze keeps its cells from freezing.
Some survive minus 16 degrees Celsius, and in one study frogs stayed frozen for two months.
In spring the heart and brain thaw first. Within about ten hours, the frog is working again.
Heart stopped. Brain on hold. Then it just hops away.

description:
Wood frogs freeze solid in winter, and then walk away in spring.
Their hearts and breathing stop while ice forms around their organs, and a glucose antifreeze protects their cells.
When it warms up, the heart and brain thaw first and the frog is moving again within about ten hours.
Would you try this if you could? Comment below.
first_comment: Alaskan wood frogs survived freezing down to minus 16 Celsius in one study. Would you freeze yourself for a winter if you knew you'd wake up?
